sections.overview: Cardium costatum is a large marine cockle of the tropical eastern Atlantic, especially documented along West Africa.
sections.identification: Adults are reported at about 80–110 mm; the inflated shell bears strong radial ribs, the feature behind its common name.
sections.habitat: Records place it on shallow sandy to muddy bottoms along the West African Atlantic coast, including the waters off Côte d’Ivoire.
sections.diet: A two-year study of 400 Ivorian specimens found a plankton-feeding diet, especially phytoplankton, with detritus and bacteria also consumed.
sections.behavior: Like other cockles, it is a shallow-burrowing bivalve that filters suspended food from water; species-specific behavioral observations are limited.
sections.reproduction: Its larval and reproductive biology is poorly covered in the sources located, so no detailed breeding schedule is given here.
sections.ecology: The accepted name is Cardium costatum; the 2007 taxonomic literature clarified its identity against the similar West African C. maxicostatum.
sections.conservation: No species-level conservation assessment was located; occurrence records and fisheries information are too limited here to infer population security.
